title: Dashboard not loading on iOS/OSX safari
body:
**What happened**:
I've received some feedback from users of my website that a few weeks ago (somewhere in December) dashboards stopped loading on iOS devices.
Sometimes whole page doesn't load, other times there is a long `Fetching` status which ends by `Grafana has failed to load its application files` error.
As far as I know, this issue occurs on iPhones and iPads on Safari and Google Chrome browsers. On macOS it works fine.


**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Unfortunately, I do not have iPhone or iPad so I cannot provide more details by myself. However, my Grafana instance is publicly available: https://stacjameteommz.pl. You should be able to test that by yourself on some iOS device.
Grafana is hosted behind reverse proxy on the server.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
My public website is based on Grafana 7.5.4, however, I've noticed the same issue with online iOS test devices on my test environment which is hosted on the newest Grafana 9.4.0-beta1.

**Environment**:
- Grafana version: 7.5.4 - 9.4.0-beta1
- Data source type & version:  InfluxDB1 (InfluxQL) on Grafana 7.5.4, InfluxDB2 (Flux) on Grafana 9.4.0-beta1
- OS Grafana is installed on: Debian
- User OS & Browser: iOS; Safari and Google Chrome. Unfortunately I don't know exact system & browser versions
- Grafana plugins: `D3 Gauge v0.0.8`, `Influx Admin v0.0.5`, `Radar Graph v1.4.4`, `WindRose v.0.7.0`, `CompareQueries v1.0.0`
- Others: -

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi @reporter,

Thanks for opening this issue.

So this is the [link](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/installation/#supported-web-browsers) which lists the supported browsers and Safari is included. (however, I am not sure myself if the iOS version of safari is also covered or not).

But as the link do says that JavaScript needs to be enabled to work properly with Grafana so please check it.

I will try to get some more information from the team about the iOS part.

For the versioning, I see that your test env. is using the 9.4.beta version. Please try to use the latest stable version as Grafana v.7 is no longer supported.

comments.body:
Hi @participant1,

Thanks for the suggestions. As I said, it's hard for me to investigate this issue in detail, as I do not have iOS device myself, but I'm pretty sure that JS is enabled in every browser by default, including Safari, so the users should be able to access Grafana on their devices without any changes in browser settings.

A few weeks ago I've had a temporary access to an iPhone on which I've tested my dev environment on stable Grafana version, I believe it was 9.3.2. It wasn't working either. Login page was loading successfuly, however, after logging in the dashboard has failed to load.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Ok, 

Can you please do the following:

Change the default log level to debug mode. To do this go to the server where grafana is installed and edit the configuration file (/etc/grafana//grafana.ini)
There you will this section;

```
#################################### Logging ##########################
[log]
# Either "console", "file", "syslog". Default is console and  file
# Use space to separate multiple modes, e.g. "console file"
;mode = console file

# Either "debug", "info", "warn", "error", "critical", default is "info"
;level = info
```
Set the parameter level to debug and remove the colon in the beginning i.e.

`level = debug`

Then restart the grafana service and try to reproduce this issue again on iOS (but using the newer ver 9.4 on your test env) by asking your friends or colleagues to open it on iOS device.

Once the website does not load, provide us with the backend logs (the default location in Linux is `/var/log/grafana/grafana.log`) so that we can have more information about the error message.

Hi,

I got access to a real IPhone device and I managed to get logs from the server when trying to enter my website from an IPhone.  The website was not loading indeed. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to use developer tools and get logs from the Safari browser itself.

The first unusual thing that I've noticed for now are the `Bad Request` queries to `/api/ds/query`. They also happen on Windows and Google Chrome:
```
logger=tsdb.influx_flux t=2023-04-30T00:23:25.705658078+02:00 level=warn msg="Flux query failed" err="invalid: error @1:1-1:5: undefined identifier SHOW\n\nerror @1:6-1:15: undefined identifier RETENTION\n\nerror @1:16-1:24: undefined identifier POLICIES\n\nerror @1:25-1:27: undefined identifier on" query="SHOW RETENTION POLICIES on \"undefined\""
```

@reporter in your case it's the google tag manager, remove it (or block it in your browser e.g. via hosts file - to test) and it will run on safari, just tested it locally.

The error itself starts as and traces down to:

```
[Error] Viewport argument key "/" not recognized and ignored.

	Global Code (Script Element 4:1:102)
	insertBefore
	(anonymous function) (gtm.js:253:427)
	b (gtm.js:254:330)
	Kc (gtm.js:56:148)
	e (gtm.js:190:269)
	(anonymous function) (gtm.js:39:132)
	(anonymous function) (gtm.js:191:388)
	(anonymous function) (gtm.js:191:143)
	yq (gtm.js:192:994)
	Gq (gtm.js:196)
	Mr (gtm.js:212:275)
	Pr (gtm.js:217:199)
	Rr (gtm.js:218:135)
```

More explicitly it's the code in google tag manager that is doing:
```
var tag = document.createElement("meta");
tag.name = "viewport";
tag.content = "/";
document.head.appendChild(tag);
```
Since meta`<meta name="viewport" content="/">` is invalid content value. 

Please verify and then I think we can close this issue.
